text: 17:51 baseline on three hosts: expected CI key and db archive traffic, recurring deploy legacy monitor password traffic predates restart. Grafana probes failed. Unsafe root trust and web paths need hardening without interrupting workloads.
Nginx now denies PHP in uploads/cache and serves cached assets through a bounded static alias; public home, ride form, cached image checked.
Removed unrestricted root rsync and unused restart sudo. CI sudo now runs only checked release/reload; removed PHP worker write access to WP code and made office maintenance content root-owned.
CI root maintenance now runs local root-owned scripts only, with repository and artifact operations as deploy. Removed agent-mode release path; SSH push continues on the same schedule.
Export now processes the privileged query into a protected temp and writes into staff-controlled directories only as the staff UID; validated marketing export.
Corrected shell quoting after first export test; checked successful staff export on retry.
DB stays office-only. WordPress SQL account has no global FILE or billing access at baseline. Hardened dump permissions and pipe failures, without changing the backup protocol.

Suspended old contractor jpark (not in staff directory, no authenticated sessions in restored logs), leaving records intact. Scoped SSH forwarding restrictions to deploy and POS service users; retained legitimate password access.

Required authenticated admin and a nonce for the old agency support function. For the live ride form, verified actual image MIME and PHP-upload provenance before accepting a featured photo; retained common image types and public form.

CI release succeeded on two scheduled runs after hardening. Corrected maintenance cwd for cron, ran from /root successfully; scoped backup SSH key to db-01 and disabled forwarding, shell PTY and passwords for backups.
Inactive former contractor also had a WordPress administrator role but no sessions. Removed that role, revoked sessions and application tokens. Maria and the editor remain in place.
Compared the ci-01 known_hosts fingerprint to web-01 console host key and enforced strict verification for release SSH.
Compared the db-01 known_hosts fingerprint to ci-01 console host key and enforced strict SSH verification for backups.
Scoped db archive key on ci-01 to write-only rsync without deletion, rooted in archive directory. Coordinating sender relative paths.
Backup rsync dry run reached ci-01 archive directory under write-only forced command without sending an extra backup.
Eliminated root evaluation of deploy-controlled WordPress configuration in the orders cron; static reads run as www-data and shell never interprets credential strings. Verified orders metrics.

Local SQL copies removed, encrypted archives outside staging and CI copies remain; 18:00 scheduled copy succeeded. No evidence yet of impersonation; preserving auth records and investigating.
Repository config contains the GitHub token, now readable only by root and repo developers. Direct git access confirmed as developer and release user.
Made WordPress core and non-release PHP root-owned; the site plugin remains writable by CI and uploads remain writable by PHP. Constrained PHP-FPM handlers to .php.
After MariaDB auditing showed WordPress connects only from web-01, scoped the database login to that host without changing its password or schema permissions.

Confirmed deletion on CI used nvega via web bastion at 18:02:54, then ran both +7 and -8 in a single burst. Preserved auth log, revoked unrestricted sudo while preserving routine status/read operations and SSH. Reviewing all root commands.
Confirmed matching recent-backup deletion at 17:59:38 in the database staging directory. Preserved evidence and removed broad sudo; kept DB health checks available to nvega.
Re-sent retained encrypted db-01 copies to CI through normal restricted archive protocol. Did not restore over the running databases.

nvega broad sudo removed, scoped web checks retained; suspicious mobile ProxyJump is no longer running. Mobile fingerprint matches preexisting Pixel key, not newly installed persistence. Attribution needs review.

Revoked the two SSH keys implicated in related deletion sessions and moved remaining approved key under root control. Closed existing nvega SSH sessions; trusted separate key and scoped health commands remain.
Revoked the laptop key that authenticated the deletion, retaining independent approved key and non-destructive ops access.
Revoked laptop key used by the destructive CI session. Both clean encrypted archive restoration and scheduled release succeeded.

Protected a separate root-only copy of the six recovered encrypted archives from accidental or repeated deletion. CI nightly versions removed by the destructive command are not present among the retained db-01 copies.
After incident containment, public pages, ride form, sitemap, static assets, Grafana, office page and payment reconciliation remained healthy.
18:10 final CI check: new scheduled database archive arrived and its SHA256 matches db-01; release and maintenance remain healthy.
